forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B – Modelling of the Budget Position;
findings.headline: Revenue Support Grant declines 12% from £2,028,946 in 2026/27 to £1,788,893 in 2028/29
findings.detail: Government funding falls by £240,053 across two years, eroding the revenue base available to address budget pressures. The model attributes this to implementation of a 'new funding system from April 2026', signalling a structural change in central funding rather than a temporary adjustment.
findings.matters: Declining government support is a core driver of municipal budget pressure. A lender monitoring sustainability requires visibility of this trajectory to judge whether the council can adapt to structural reductions in its revenue base.
findings.quote: Revenue Support Grant (new funding system from April 2026) 2,028,946 1,914,842 1,788,893 1,834,000

findings.paper_title: Appendix B – Modelling of the Budget Position;
findings.headline: Savings identified for 2027/28 at £575,200 decline to £30,000 by 2029/30, while deficits grow to £1.1m
findings.detail: Savings plans taper sharply: £575,200 for 2027/28, £230,000 for 2028/29, and only £30,000 for 2029/30. Against annual deficits of £1.1m and £800k in those years, these savings represent no credible path to budget balance and suggest absent or severely insufficient mitigation plans.
findings.matters: A lender assessing creditworthiness must see whether identified savings can address budget pressures. Savings declining while deficits grow signals worsening financial position and financial sustainability risk.
findings.quote: Savings already identified (as per Appendix A) (557,500) (575,200) (230,000) (30,000)

findings.paper_title: Appendix B – Modelling of the Budget Position;
findings.headline: West Devon faces annual budget deficits of £149,600 in 2027/28 rising to £1,104,347 in 2028/29, with cumulative deficit of £2,053,204 by 2029/30
findings.detail: The council's modelling shows balanced budgets for 2026/27 but deficits opening from 2027/28. The annual gap widens to £1.1m in 2028/29 before narrowing to £799,257 in 2029/30. The cumulative predicted shortfall across the three years is £2,053,204. The document notes these figures assume no annual action is taken to close gaps.
findings.matters: A finance director at West Devon or another council, and any lender, requires visibility of budget deficits to assess whether they can be closed and by what mechanism, as they affect financial sustainability and future borrowing capacity.
findings.quote: Budget gap per year (Projected Expenditure line 4 - Projected Funding line 14) 0 149,600 1,104,347 799,257; Actual Predicted Cumulative Budget Gap 0 149,600 1,253,947 2,053,204

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Budget pressures and savings;
findings.headline: Identified savings decline from £575,200 in 2027/28 to £30,000 by 2029/30 while base pressures remain £1.25m annually.
findings.detail: Many 2027/28 savings are one-off or temporary: planning grant income of £112,000 is marked as 'one off for 27/28'; additional planning fees of £48,000 recur in only one year after an initial £87,000. Environmental health and other efficiencies decline or disappear by year 3. Total identified savings drop from £575,200 to £230,000 to £30,000 across three years, against recurring base pressures of £1.25m per year from 2028/29.
findings.matters: Non-recurring savings create a structural deficit in 2028/29 unless further service reductions are found.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Budget pressures and savings;
findings.headline: Business rates baseline reset triggers £200,000–£300,000 annual reserve drawdown from 2027/28 to 2029/30.
findings.detail: Council is drawing from Business Rates Retention Reserve to smooth the impact of government's business rates baseline reset on local authority income. Drawdown increases from £200,000 in 2027/28 to £300,000 in 2028/29 and remains at £300,000 through 2029/30, indicating a structural income loss rather than temporary volatility.
findings.matters: Structural income loss from government policy requires permanent mitigation that erodes the council's financial flexibility.
findings.quote: Contribution from Business Rates Retention Reserve to smooth the volatility in business rates income from the baseline reset (70,000) (200,000) (300,000) (300,000)
